A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same research lineage despite the changed title: the backbone, video corpus, ranking framework, and several result rows match. The supplied text, figures, tables, and equations are readable, including v3's Appendices A-D. v1 references a separate supplement that is not included; judgments concern the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot evaluations, supervised fine-tuning results, and component ablations in Tables 2-4.

after.justification: v3 reports original component and iterative-training results in Table 1, plus individual-teacher student experiments and a supervised-student control in Figure 4 and Appendix Table 5.

M1.justification: v3 adds difficult-sample selection through teacher-student gMAD disagreement and misclassified synthetic-distortion pairs (Section 4.2). It also adds an entropy-based confidence loss with adaptive weighting (Section 4.3, Appendix C.2.2), beyond v1's standard supervised fine-tuning objective. These substantially change training, while the core visual architecture and anchor-based scoring remain.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same web-video sources, authentic and synthetic distortion categories, and ten evaluation splits spanning UGC, gaming, high-frame-rate, and compression scenarios. PLVD is renamed Dw2s, with the same 438k-video and 700k-pair totals. The new teacher-student experiments reuse this coverage; additional dataset descriptions do not establish new domains or benchmarks.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains MinimalisticVQA VII/IX, FAST-VQA, DOVER, and Q-Align, but adds evaluated VQA2 and VQAThinker baselines. It removes the six opinion-unaware comparators reported in v1 Table 2, including NIQE, IL-NIQE, VIIDEO, STEM, TPQI, and BUONA-VISTA. v1's separate supervised fine-tuning comparison also disappears.

E3.justification: The reported sampling target changes from aggregated distributions of four UGC datasets to LSVQ alone. For ranking training, v1 specifies learning rate 1e-5 and total batch size 4; v3 Appendix C.2.1 specifies 1e-4 and batch size 2 per device. v3 separately introduces a 200k-video single-teacher protocol with 200k iterations and a supervised-student control, while removing v1's downstream fine-tuning protocol. These documented changes do not establish that retained result rows were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds individual-teacher generalization diagnostics and an isolated confidence-loss comparison through models II and III. It retains the synthetic-distortion contribution comparison, but removes v1's hard-versus-soft ranking comparison, motion-encoder ablation, and equal-data control testing label refinement against merely adding samples. The questions isolated by the analyses therefore change substantially.

E5.justification: v1 Table 3 explicitly reports ten-fold cross-validation for KoNViD-1k, LIVE-VQC, and YouTube-UGC; that evaluation and its resampling information are absent from v3. Neither version reports seed-wise variability, confidence intervals, or performance significance tests. v3's confidence loss concerns training, not statistical uncertainty in evaluation.

E6.justification: v3 model II repeats v1's Stage 1 soft-ranking scores, but later-stage results change substantially. Reported final-model overall OOD SRCC/PLCC changes from 0.716/0.752 to 0.745/0.789; in-domain results change from 0.861/0.868 to 0.865/0.872. These involve revised models and protocols, not established same-setting gains. Table 5 adds individual-teacher student results, while the earlier fine-tuning and several ablation results disappear.

T1.justification: v3 introduces a formal constrained gMAD selection rule (Equation 1) and mathematical definitions for the entropy objective and adaptive weighting (Equations 23-26). These extend the methodological formalism without adding a theorem or proof framework. The retained feature-fusion equations and expanded description of previously used MAP inference do not establish a new theoretical foundation.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from a large pairwise-labeled dataset and ranking-based self-supervision to demonstrating and improving weak-to-strong generalization. v3 explicitly foregrounds learning beyond individual teachers and difficulty-guided iterative training. It drops v1's abstract-level claim of state-of-the-art performance after human-labeled fine-tuning, while retaining strong in-domain and OOD performance claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations involving larger pseudo-labeled datasets, noisy supervision, confidence reinforcement, and teacher-student disagreement, together with a VQA foundation-model outlook. It removes v1's explanation of the LIVE-VQC performance gap and its explicit limitation that comparison against five anchors substantially increases inference time, although multi-anchor inference remains.

D1.justification: Appendices A-C newly document distortion parameters and encoding settings, preprocessing resolution, model sizes, optimizer details, confidence-loss scheduling, and probability-to-score calculations. These are largely additional disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to previously unspecified settings. v3 supplies a code repository address instead of only promising release, but no longer specifies v1's minimum-variance anchor-selection rule.

R1.justification: v3 replaces the dataset-centered related-work subsection with substantial weak-to-strong positioning, citing Burns, Guo, Liu and Alahi, and Sang, and adds a ranking-method discussion. It newly attributes the student architecture to LMM-VQA and discusses newer VQA competitors. This changes the paper's intellectual positioning beyond citation maintenance.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around weak-to-strong learning. The original dataset-method-experiments progression becomes an initial W2S investigation followed by an enhanced framework, with technical material moved into appendices and a new Discussion section.

P2.justification: v3 changes the two-column presentation to a single-column technical report, redistributes the original composite overview, and redraws the architecture and iterative-training diagrams. Dataset statistics and distribution plots move into the appendix; distortion illustrations, model-size and dataset-description tables, and the teacher-student results display are added. The main comparison table is substantially restructured, while the former fine-tuning and dedicated ablation tables disappear.

improvement.justification: v3 directly supports its revised W2S claim through individual-teacher student comparisons and a supervised-student control (Table 5), while Appendices A-C make data generation, training, and inference substantially more inspectable. These improve evidential clarity and reproducibility. The net gain is limited by removing v1's equal-data label-refinement control and explicit inference-cost limitation, leaving the iterative mechanism less cleanly isolated.
